html:
The Wailaki are one of the Eel River Athapaskan peoples of northwestern California, living along the Eel River in what are now Mendocino and Humboldt counties. Their language is part of the Athabaskan family, related to languages spoken far away in Alaska and by the Apache and Navajo.

They lived in small village groups, fishing for salmon, gathering acorns and hunting. In the 1850s and 1860s settlers and militias killed many Wailaki in the California genocide, and survivors were sent to the Round Valley Reservation, which they share with the Yuki, Pomo and others. Their neighbours to the north included the Tsnungwe.
